title: System identification campaign - Skywalker X8 UAV
access: Full public access to DataverseNO Version 1.0 under CC0 1.0 Universal. DOI 10.18710/U4TLYV, version number, file IDs, and MD5 checksums form the immutable citation and integrity contract; retrieved 2026-08-06.
topics: Measured Skywalker X8 UAV system-identification campaign with 17 independent maneuvers and creator-designated training/validation folders.
Nine-file longitudinal subset: seven training and two validation records using 3211 elevator sequences and elevator doublets.
Headerless 41-column, nominal 40 Hz record contract with explicit channel names and units.
Manual synchronization/resampling of multirate IMU, GPS, propulsion, and command channels.
Wind, excitation, record boundaries, and channel preprocessing as limits on model interpretation.
key_results: The selected longitudinal subset has 3,828 structurally complete rows and must remain nine separate time-ordered maneuvers.
Elevator command and pitch-rate response support a low-order ARX teaching study, but the dataset authors do not supply or validate the course's proposed model.
The two untouched longitudinal validation records enable per-maneuver and aggregate one-step/free-run evaluation after every modeling choice is frozen on training data.
Neither `EstimatedState_alpha` nor any maneuver name licenses a stall label, and manual synchronization precludes an unqualified exact actuator-delay claim.
pedagogy: Anchor the module application in an actual CC0 measurement pipeline: verify the immutable source contract, preserve maneuver boundaries, freeze a modest model on creator-designated training records, then report validation behavior without a prefabricated success claim. Retain MIT perching imagery only to motivate why physical validation matters and state that it depicts a different vehicle.
figures: Creator-designated maneuver partition with independent record boundaries and state resets.
Computed Skywalker X8 validation residuals by time and excitation maneuver, generated only after deterministic code and data land.
Physical X8 to synchronized 40 Hz record to frozen model to per-maneuver validation pipeline.
gems: The nine records combine two excitation families while preserving an author-defined train/validation separation.
A 40 Hz released table built from 200, 40, and 10 Hz sources makes timing provenance part of the identification model.
A deliberately unsuccessful validation outcome remains a valid result if the protocol was frozen and per-maneuver residuals are reported.
chapter_map: Identity, rights, version, and checksums → DataverseNO Version 1.0 metadata.

One-step/free-run scoring and residual diagnosis → two longitudinal validation CSVs.
